patterns.name: Filterable list
patterns.description: Page header with one primary action, a filter bar, and a data table that handles loading, empty and error states.

patterns.name: Form page
patterns.description: Single-column form in a card: labelled fields, inline validation on submit, one primary and one secondary action.

patterns.name: Dashboard summary
patterns.description: Row of stat cards followed by cards that summarise recent activity with links to the full lists.

rules.title: Colors come from semantic tokens
rules.description: Every color in CSS, inline styles and color props is a semantic color token, var(--color-*).
rules.rationale: Literal colors drift from the palette, break theming, and hide contrast decisions from review.
rules.remediation: Replace the literal with the semantic token for its purpose (text, surface, border, action, status). If no token fits, ask the design-system team for one instead of adding a value.

rules.title: Spacing uses the spacing scale
rules.description: Margins, paddings and gaps use the --space-* tokens (or 0 and auto).
rules.rationale: A fixed 4px-based scale keeps rhythm consistent across screens and lets density change globally.
rules.remediation: Use the nearest --space-* step. For layout between components prefer <Stack gap={n}> over margins.

rules.title: Font sizes use the type scale
rules.description: font-size uses the --font-size-* tokens. Line heights and the font shorthand are not checked.
rules.rationale: Six sizes, each with a defined use, keep the hierarchy readable; one-off sizes blur it.
rules.remediation: Use the --font-size-* token for the text's role (see the typography table). If no size fits, ask the design-system owners for a token instead of adding a one-off size.

examples.note: Percentages are relative, and line heights are a different property.

rules.title: Only defined semantic tokens are referenced
rules.description: var() references point at defined semantic tokens, and tokens are defined only in the token file. Primitive --palette-* tokens are internal to the token file.
rules.rationale: Primitives describe raw values, not intent; using them bypasses theming. Misspelled tokens silently fall back to nothing.
rules.remediation: Use the semantic token that expresses the intent; the suggestion lists tokens with the same value.

rules.title: No !important in application CSS
rules.description: Application CSS never forces a declaration with !important. The design system and the token sources (src/design-system/**) are out of scope.
rules.rationale: !important overrides design-system styles and states (focus, disabled, error) from outside, and every later fix needs another !important to win.
rules.remediation: Remove !important. If the declaration then loses, use the component's variant or prop, or fix the selector's specificity or order.

examples.note: Comments and strings are not declaration flags.

rules.title: Use design-system controls
rules.description: Application code renders buttons, links, form fields and tables through design-system components, not raw HTML elements.
rules.rationale: The components carry focus handling, disabled and loading states, accessible labelling and tokens; raw elements lose all of that.
rules.remediation: Replace the raw element with the design-system component named in the finding.

examples.code:
import { Button } from '../design-system';
export const A = () => <Button>Save</Button>;

rules.title: Component contracts are satisfied
rules.description: Design-system components get their required props and only approved values, including the props that drive loading, empty and error states.
rules.rationale: A data table without status or empty-state props renders a blank area while loading or when there is no data.
rules.remediation: Pass the missing prop or use an approved value; the component catalog lists each contract.

examples.code:
import { DataTable } from '../design-system';
export const T = () => <DataTable columns={[]} rows={[]} />;

import { Badge } from '../design-system';
export const B = () => <Badge tone="success">Paid</Badge>;

rules.title: Reuse existing components before creating new ones
rules.description: New components should not re-implement something the design system already provides.
rules.rationale: Parallel implementations diverge in states, accessibility and visual details.
rules.remediation: Use or compose the existing component. If the new component is genuinely different, rename it and explain why in the pull request.

rules.title: New patterns are reviewed
rules.description: Changed components are compared with reference patterns and existing components. Novel patterns are allowed but need a design review.
rules.rationale: New patterns are how the system grows; reviewing them keeps growth deliberate instead of accidental.
rules.remediation: Link the guidance that justifies the pattern in the pull request, or reuse the nearest reference pattern.

rules.title: Shared design-system changes need owner review
rules.description: Changes to tokens or design-system components are reported with their downstream usages and need review by the design-system owners.
rules.rationale: A one-line token change can restyle every screen; the people who own the system should see the blast radius.
rules.remediation: Request review from @acme/design-system and check the affected screens in the visual diff.

rules.title: Visual changes are reviewed
rules.description: Rendered screens that differ from the base revision are shown for human review. A difference is not a violation by itself.
rules.rationale: Screenshots catch effects that source analysis cannot attribute, such as a token change cascading through many screens.
rules.remediation: Confirm each highlighted region is intended.

rules.title: No new automated accessibility violations
rules.description: axe-core (WCAG 2.x A and AA rules) runs on every captured state. Violations that the base revision did not have are shown for review.
rules.rationale: Components come accessible by default; a change that adds a contrast, label or landmark problem works around them.
rules.remediation: Fix the element axe names (the rule link explains how), or confirm in review that it is a false positive.

rules.title: One primary action per view
rules.description: Each page or dialog has at most one primary button; other actions use secondary or ghost buttons.
rules.rationale: Several primary buttons compete for attention and make the main task unclear.
rules.remediation: Keep the main action primary and demote the others to secondary or ghost.

rules.title: States are complete and explained
rules.description: Views that load data handle loading, empty and error states, and their copy says what happened and what to do next.
rules.rationale: Missing or vague states leave users stuck; most support tickets start at an empty or failed screen.
rules.remediation: Add the missing state and write copy that names the cause and the next step.

rules.title: New patterns build on existing guidance
rules.description: A new pattern composes existing components and tokens and follows the documented principles, rather than introducing a parallel visual language.
rules.rationale: Novelty is fine when it extends the system coherently.
rules.remediation: Compose from design-system components and explain the need in the pull request.

exceptions.reason: The partner promo uses the partner's contractual brand colors; it is removed when the campaign ends.
